one_month_reasoning: No Netflix earnings fall in the window to 2026-12-17 (Q4 FY2026 results come in mid/late January 2027 with the first FY2027 guide). In the window: Nielsen's next Gauge release, Antenna monthly data on US sign-ups after the 2026 price change, the Q4 content slate (final Emily in Paris season, the Fury-Joshua fight) and holiday ad demand; the NFL Christmas games fall after the window. None is a scheduled repricing event, and the stock sits at its 52-week low after a -46% year with no new news since the Oct 20 print. Momentum and post-miss drift argue mildly down, oversold reversal mildly up; we stay neutral: lognormal centred on $59.68 with monthly vol 36% / 3.5 = 10.3%.

fair_value.method: NTM P/E 16.59x (peer median 17.66x shrunk toward NFLX's 16.33x with k = 0.8) on our own NTM GAAP EPS of ~$4.09 at 2027-11-17 (mostly FY2028 EPS $4.27, 3.7% below the $4.43 consensus), from a quarterly UCAN/International revenue build (FY2027 +8.3%, FY2028 +7.6%) and content-amortization/cost build (EBIT margin 32.6% / 33.3%).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at horizon ~$4.09 (engine, 3,985M shares at H) x 16.59x

inputs_detail.derivation: Whole-company peer median NTM P/E = median(DIS 16.64, SONY 17.66, SPOT 38.86) = 17.66x (peers.md 2026-11-18 refresh). NFLX own NTM P/E 16.33x on the same Zacks basis. Exit = 17.66 x (16.33 / 17.66)^0.8 = 16.59x (k = 0.8, the tested default; no reason for a different k: earnings are not distorted in the NTM window since the termination fee sits in FY2026 Q1).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Including META and GOOGL (attention platforms; segment-only for Netflix's ads, 5% of revenue) gives a 18.56x median and 17.1x exit, +3% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: UCAN = paid members x ARM. Members: Antenna data (Reuters, source 9) show monthly US subscriber losses through September 2026 and no net adds in 2026; Netflix disputes it, so we take members at about -0.5% y/y through 2027 and ~0% in 2028 (not the steeper decline Antenna implies). ARM: the 2026 US price change landed in Q2'26 ('partial-quarter impact', Q2'26 letter, source 4) and Q3'26 UCAN grew +11.0% with flat members, so ARM ~+11% until the change laps: Q4'26 +11.0%, Q1'27 +9.5%, Q2'27 +7.5% (partial lap). After the lap ARM growth = ads + plan mix only: Netflix ads ~$2.7B in 2026 (source 14) growing to ~$4.2B in 2027 adds ~2.5-3 pts in UCAN where ads are concentrated, so H2'27 +4.5%. Netflix's US price steps came in Jan 2025 and spring 2026 (sources 6, 4), ~15 months apart, so we place the next one in early 2028: Q1'28 +5.5%, Q2-Q3'28 +7.0%, Q4'28 +6.5% (ads maturing). Other evidence-based builds: (a) Antenna's no-net-adds reading taken at face value as members -2% a year: UCAN FY2027 growth ~4.5% instead of ~6.4%; (b) a second US price change in H2 2027 (Netflix's 15-month cadence from spring 2026): FY2027 UCAN ~+8%; (c) Spotify's Q3'26 ARPU +7.5% cc on price increases with 6M net adds (source 21) shows subscription price power still works in a mature market. The upside and downside cases move this driver by +2.5 / -3.5 pts.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Antenna's member losses taken literally (-2%/yr) cut FY2027 UCAN to ~+4.5% and the research target (12m) by ~4%; a 2027 US price step lifts it ~+5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3'26 International grew +12.6% reported, ~+10.9% F/X neutral (EMEA 9%, LATAM 12%, APAC 15% F/X neutral, weighted by Q3 revenue; source 1). We hold F/X flat from here, so reported ~ F/X neutral after Q4'26. Members: APAC/India view hours +24% and India revenue +18% (source 1), and the ad tier launches in 15 more countries from March 2027 (9 EMEA + Colombia, Peru, New Zealand first; source 14), so members grow ~5-6% in 2027. ARM +3-4% from the H1'26 price changes in Mexico and Spain lapping and ads. Path: Q4'26 +12.0% (some F/X tailwind left), 2027 +10.5% / +10.0% / +9.5% / +9.0% (decelerating as the 2026 price changes lap), 2028 +8.5% and +8.0% in Q4 (ad-tier countries in the base). Other evidence-based builds: (a) hold the Q3'26 F/X-neutral +10.9% through 2027: FY2027 International ~+11% instead of ~+9.7%; (b) EMEA's slower F/X-neutral 9% across all regions as markets mature (Greenlight/Hub on churn, source 24): ~+8.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Holding the Q3'26 F/X-neutral ~10.9% through 2027 adds ~+2% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4'26 5,250 = +10.2% y/y: Netflix guided FY2026 content amortization ~+10% (Q2'26 letter, source 4), which needs Q4 ~5,300; Q3'26 grew only +5.8% and 'higher growth in H1 than H2', so slightly below the guide-implied Q4 (FY2026 17,965, +9.4%). 2027 +6.5% and 2028 +6.0% per quarter: content cash spend runs ~1.1x amortization (source 1), the new content chief and ~6% headcount cut point to discipline, while live sports (three NFL games in Q4'26, source 9/Reuters) and the Paramount+HBO Max combination (~200M subs, source 18) bid up rights. Other builds: (a) ~+10% a year as in 2026 (rights inflation): FY2027 EBIT -$0.65B; (b) +5.8% (Q3'26 run-rate): +$0.12B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Content amortization growing ~10% a year (rights inflation after the Paramount-WBD merger) cuts FY2028 EBIT ~$1.3B, ~-7% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 actual ratios 33.3% / 32.3% / 32.5% ran ~1 pt above 2025's 32.0% / 31.3% / 31.6% ex Brazil (ad-tech, live and games build-out). Q4'26 35.3%: Q4'25 35.9% held Q4 marketing and WBD deal costs; +1.2 pts restructuring in Q4'26 (source 1) less the absent deal costs and underlying 2026 creep; this gives Q4'26 EBIT ~$3.45B vs the $3.50B guide, i.e. slightly below, because Q1-Q3 beats were 'timing of expenses' (sources 4, 1) that fall into Q4. 2027: each 2026 quarter -0.3 pt (the ~1,000-job / ~6% headcount cut, Reuters source 9, ~$0.3B a year, partly reinvested in ad sales and tech), Q4'27 also drops the 1.2 pt restructuring. 2028: a further -0.2 pt (scale). Other builds: (a) no savings (2026 creep continues +0.5 pt): FY2027 EBIT -$0.45B; (b) full $0.3B savings kept (-0.55 pt): +$0.14B.
inputs_detail.variant_view: No headcount savings (2026's ~+1 pt creep continues at +0.5 pt) is ~-3% to the research target (12m).

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM interest expense 856.9 / total debt 15,132.4 = 5.66%.

anchor.note: gross interest over gross debt; interest income on the $8.2B cash is not netted, the conservative reading.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Cross-check only: consensus NTM EPS at the horizon ~$4.35 (FY2027 $3.74 x ~0.12 + FY2028 $4.43 x ~0.88, Nasdaq/Zacks) x 16.59x

inputs_detail.derivation: Nasdaq (Zacks) consensus page, retrieved 2026-11-18; NTM weight by days in the window Nov 2027-Nov 2028.

downside.story: P10: Antenna's US member losses are real and deepen (members -3% a year), the next US price step slips or is cut back, YouTube keeps taking TV time (15.8% vs Netflix 7.7% in Nielsen's August Gauge) and ads stall near $3.5B in 2027; International slows to the EMEA-like 7-8%; the ad build-out keeps non-content costs ~0.8 pt higher. FY2027 revenue ~+5%, EBIT margin ~31%, and the market prices Netflix like a mature media company at ~13.3x NTM EPS (below DIS 16.6x).

base.story: Median: UCAN growth slows from ~11% to ~4.5% once the 2026 price change laps in mid-2027 (members ~flat per Antenna), International ~9-10% on ad-tier launches in 15 countries, ads ~$4.2B in 2027; margins expand ~1 pt a year from content-amortization leverage and the headcount cut; ~4% a year of share count retired; P/E holds ~16.6x.

upside.story: P90: a second US price step lands in H2 2027 with churn holding at ~2% (Antenna), the ad stack catches up (ads toward the $5-6B 2027 forecasts) and the 15 new ad countries ramp; FY2027 revenue ~+11%, margin ~34%, and the multiple re-rates toward the META/GOOGL attention platforms (~19x).

comps_summary.peer_range: 16.6x (DIS) - 38.9x (SPOT) NTM P/E for whole-company peers; META 18.6x and GOOGL 19.3x are segment-only

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount is argued beyond the k = 0.8 shrink: Netflix's current discount to DIS/SONY/SPOT reflects the engagement and US-member evidence (Nielsen, Antenna, Apptopia) and the WARC-style ad hopes being cut; 81-85% of a P/E gap persists a year out in the tested sample, so we keep most of it.

Genuine global subscription-video peers are few: WBD is being absorbed by Paramount Skydance (source 18), PSKY is mid-merger with distorted earnings, ROKU and other CTV names are near-zero earners on a different model, AMZN's Prime Video is a small part of AMZN, and China/Korea/India video names are excluded by rule.

no_peers.why: Listed subscription media peers exist, though few.

fit.why: Netflix's whole business is subscription streaming of studio content
Netflix ads ~$2.7B of ~$51.1B; segment-only, not in the median

thesis_triggers.check: Regional table and FY2027 guide in the Q4 FY2026 8-K ex 99.1; Reuters/Antenna coverage of US net adds

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: content amortization +2 pts a year faster, ~4% lower NTM EPS from 2029 (~$2.7 a share at the horizon)

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: UCAN revenue growth ~3 pts lower a year; carried in the downside case

reverse_dcf_check: 16.6x NTM P/E (a 6.0% earnings yield, nearly all returned via buybacks) at a ~9-10% cost of equity implies ~3.5-4% perpetual earnings growth after 2028, e.g. revenue growth fading from ~7% to ~4% by the early 2030s with EBIT margins holding ~34-35%; plausible given the YouTube and rights-inflation risks above, which keep it below the 2026 +13% pace.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT and EPS are after SBC (1.1% of revenue TTM, F46); the share count falls only by buybacks net of option dilution (-3.8% a year), so SBC is counted once. Peers' Zacks NTM EPS: DIS and META/GOOGL per peers.md basis notes.

reasoning: Industry lane. The chain says Netflix's demand is flat in the US and still growing abroad: Antenna (via Reuters) shows no US net adds through September 2026, Apptopia shows non-openers up 16.6% y/y, H1 view hours rose only 2%, and YouTube holds 2x Netflix's TV time in Nielsen's Gauge. Pricing still works (Q3 UCAN +11% on the spring price change; Spotify's +7.5% cc ARPU shows the subscription model holds), but the US price step laps in Q2 2027. Competitors: Disney's streaming profit doubled (11.5% margin) and Paramount will merge HBO Max with Paramount+ (~200M subs), both raising content-rights pressure; YouTube's own ad growth slowed to 9%, so the CTV ad pool is not booming for anyone, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad outlook 10% to $2.7B. Build: two-region quarterly revenue (UCAN growth 11% -> ~4.5% in H2 2027 -> ~7% in 2028 with a next price step; International ~10% -> 8.5%), content amortization +6.5%/+6%, non-content costs down ~0.3 pt on the headcount cut. FY2027 revenue $55.4B (+8.3%) is below the 'sustained double-digit' aim; FY2027 EPS $3.73 matches the $3.74 consensus because our margin is higher, and FY2028 EPS $4.27 is 3.7% below the $4.43 consensus. Value: P/E 16.59x (whole-company peers DIS/SONY/SPOT median 17.66x shrunk to NFLX's 16.33x, k = 0.8) on NTM EPS ~$4.09 gives the research target (12m). Downside (P10) and upside (P90) move the regional growth drivers, costs and the multiple; the left tail is wider, matching the -46% year. Outside ad forecasts (WARC Feb 2026, Motley Fool Sept 2026) were overtaken by the Oct 20 cut and are reconciled, not used as the path. Research was limited by blocked consensus pages (no revenue consensus) and paywalled trade press (Puck, MediaPost).

inputs_detail.derivation: UCAN = paid members x ARM. Members: Antenna data (Reuters, source 9) show monthly US subscriber losses through September 2026 and no net adds in 2026; Netflix disputes it, so we take members at about -0.5% y/y through 2027 and ~0% in 2028 (not the steeper decline Antenna implies). ARM: the 2026 US price change landed in Q2'26 ('partial-quarter impact', Q2'26 letter, source 4) and Q3'26 UCAN grew +11.0% with flat members, so ARM ~+11% until the change laps: Q4'26 +11.0%, Q1'27 +9.5%, Q2'27 +7.5% (partial lap). After the lap ARM growth = ads + plan mix only: Netflix ads ~$2.7B in 2026 (source 14) growing to ~$4.2B in 2027 adds ~2.5-3 pts in UCAN where ads are concentrated, so H2'27 +4.5%. Netflix's US price steps came in Jan 2025 and spring 2026 (sources 6, 4), ~15 months apart, so we place the next one in early 2028: Q1'28 +5.5%, Q2-Q3'28 +7.0%, Q4'28 +6.5% (ads maturing). Other evidence-based builds: (a) Antenna's no-net-adds reading taken at face value as members -2% a year: UCAN FY2027 growth ~4.5% instead of ~6.4%; (b) a second US price change in H2 2027 (Netflix's 15-month cadence from spring 2026): FY2027 UCAN ~+8%; (c) Spotify's Q3'26 ARPU +7.5% cc on price increases with 6M net adds (source 21) shows subscription price power still works in a mature market. The upside and downside cases move this driver by +2.5 / -3.5 pts.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Antenna's member losses taken literally (-2%/yr) cut FY2027 UCAN to ~+4.5% and the research target (12m) by ~4%; a 2027 US price step lifts it ~+5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3'26 International grew +12.6% reported, ~+10.9% F/X neutral (EMEA 9%, LATAM 12%, APAC 15% F/X neutral, weighted by Q3 revenue; source 1). We hold F/X flat from here, so reported ~ F/X neutral after Q4'26. Members: APAC/India view hours +24% and India revenue +18% (source 1), and the ad tier launches in 15 more countries from March 2027 (9 EMEA + Colombia, Peru, New Zealand first; source 14), so members grow ~5-6% in 2027. ARM +3-4% from the H1'26 price changes in Mexico and Spain lapping and ads. Path: Q4'26 +12.0% (some F/X tailwind left), 2027 +10.5% / +10.0% / +9.5% / +9.0% (decelerating as the 2026 price changes lap), 2028 +8.5% and +8.0% in Q4 (ad-tier countries in the base). Other evidence-based builds: (a) hold the Q3'26 F/X-neutral +10.9% through 2027: FY2027 International ~+11% instead of ~+9.7%; (b) EMEA's slower F/X-neutral 9% across all regions as markets mature (Greenlight/Hub on churn, source 24): ~+8.5%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Holding the Q3'26 F/X-neutral ~10.9% through 2027 adds ~+2% to the research target (12m).

Other builds: (a) ~+10% a year as in 2026 (rights inflation): FY2027 EBIT -$0.65B; (b) +5.8% (Q3'26 run-rate): +$0.12B.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount is argued beyond the k = 0.8 shrink: Netflix's current discount to DIS/SONY/SPOT reflects the engagement and US-member evidence (Nielsen, Antenna, Apptopia) and the WARC-style ad hopes being cut; 81-85% of a P/E gap persists a year out in the tested sample, so we keep most of it.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 3 whole-company peers (DIS, SONY, SPOT) + 2 segment-only (META, GOOGL). Genuine global subscription-video peers are few: WBD is being absorbed by Paramount Skydance (source 18), PSKY is mid-merger with distorted earnings, ROKU and other CTV names are near-zero earners on a different model, AMZN's Prime Video is a small part of AMZN, and China/Korea/India video names are excluded by rule.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly two-region build: UCAN and International revenue are lines with reported history, each grown y/y by its driver (members x ARM incl. ads, argued from Antenna, the price-change calendar and the ad outlook); EBIT = revenue x (1 - non-content cost ratio) - content amortization. Netflix reports one operating segment, so regional EBIT is not built (no segment_build) and the regions feed total revenue. The value is carried by one leg: NTM P/E 16.59x on our own GAAP EPS at the horizon (Nov 2027-Nov 2028, mostly FY2028). No DCF (policy), no FCF-yield leg (NFLX is Communication Services, not on the tech FCF list). Consensus P/E is shown as a zero-weight cross-check.
model_inputs.gap_note: 1) Driver-set approval (Kilian 2026-11-04) was not obtained: this forecaster cannot post cards; the set (ucan_g, intl_g, content_amort, opex_ratio) goes to the supervisor as a proposal. 2) Drivers are regional revenue growth rates because Netflix stopped reporting members/ARM in 2025; members and ARM are argued inside each derivation. 3) Q4 FY2026 revenue lands on the guide from the Q3 run-rate (not set to it); Q4 margin sits below the guide. 4) Financing: none >= 20% probability; the $1B Q3 bond refinanced a Q4 maturity (source 1); no M&A financing after the WBD exit. 5) Judgment calls to size: content amortization growth (+6.5% vs ~10%, ~-7%) is the largest single alternative and may exceed 5%; the k choice is the default 0.8. 6) Twelve Data analyst estimates need a higher plan and Zacks pages were blocked, so no revenue consensus is cited; EPS consensus from Nasdaq (Zacks).
